newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist says Germany needs to be pushed.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist says Germany needs to be pushed.

text.p: The interim head of France's Socialist party said on Sunday Germany needed to be "pushed" away from preoccupation with financial criteria concerning European unity.

"Germany needs to be pushed because there are too many in Germany who worry solely about financial criteria," said Francois Hollande about a European Union summit in Amsterdam from Monday which will centre on a Franco-German row over the direction of monetary union.

"But things are changing. Today, the Belgian government is behind us and certain northern European governments understand our preoccupation with employment. (Britain's Prime Minister) Tony Blair also agrees with our position," Hollande said.

French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, whose party came to power after an upset parliamentary election victory on June 1, wants the EU to put employment as high on its list of priorties as monetary stability.

The two-day EU summit was supposed to culminate in agreement of a new treaty setting Europe's course for the future but the new Socialist-led French government wants new commitments concerning employment.
